One of the biggest struggles beginners face when starting a digital product business is deciding what to sell. You have so many ideas running through your head. You see someone selling ebooks, another person selling templates, someone else selling courses, and suddenly you want to create everything. You start asking yourself: "What if nobody buys it?" "How do I know people actually need this?" "What if I spend time creating it and it doesn't sell?" And because you're afraid of making the wrong choice, you keep researching, jumping from one idea to another, and sometimes never create anything at all. But here's what you need to understand: You don't have to create what everybody else is selling. Start by identifying a particular group of people, understanding a problem they struggle with, and finding a useful solution you can offer. Don't start with what you want to create. Start with what people need help solving. That's a much better place to begin.
